content: 1. Lurbinectedin: Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives, increase the lurbinectedin dose to the pre-coadministration level. 2. Macitentan: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases macitentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Metoprolol: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases metoprolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat is a CYP2D6 inhibitor; exercise caution with CYP2D6 substrates that have serious or life-threatening effects at elevated plasma concentrations. 4. Midostaurin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases midostaurin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 5. Mifepristone: Mifepristone increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Nefazodone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases nefazodone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat is a CYP2D6 inhibitor; caution is advised with CYP2D6 substrates that have serious or life-threatening effects at elevated plasma concentrations. 7. Nortriptyline: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases nortriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat is a CYP2D6 inhibitor; caution is advised with CYP2D6 substrates that have serious or life-threatening effects at elevated plasma concentrations. 10. Olaparib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases olaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 11. Omaveloxolone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects occur. 12. Osimertinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases osimertinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 13. Palbociclib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 14. Palovarotene: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases palovarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Pimavanserin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 16. Pirtobrutinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. Resume the previous dose after the inhibitor is discontinued for 5 half-lives. 17. Pomalidomide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Ponatinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 19. If necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose. 22. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 23. If necessary, monitor for hypotension and reduce the dose as needed. 27. Siponimod: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 28.
